sentence_stem: Had the committee studied the evidence more carefully,
correct_completion: the verdict would have been different.
full_sentence: Had the committee studied the evidence more carefully, the verdict would have been different.
acceptable_variants: the outcome could have been different.

options.text: the members were chosen last spring.
options.why_wrong: This gives an unrelated fact about the committee. The stem needs a main clause describing the hypothetical past result.

options.text: so the verdict was reached quickly.
options.why_wrong: 'So' signals a real cause and result, not the outcome of a past condition that did not happen.
'Although' sets up a contrast with a real fact, but the stem already creates an unreal past condition, so this does not complete it.

options.text: the verdict would have been different.

grammar_focus: Inverted third conditional (Had + subject + past participle)
explanation: The stem is an inverted third conditional: 'Had' replaces 'if', and the subject and auxiliary swap places. The main clause must use 'would have' with a past participle to describe the unreal past result. Learners often keep a plain past verb here, so it helps to remember the whole inverted structure.
